name: CycleWire, intent only
summary: The CycleWire app with nothing fetched ahead of intent: the core loads up front, and every action's code when someone reaches for it, Add to cart included, on touch screens too.

variant.differs: No <link rel="modulepreload"> for Add to cart, and start({ preload: 'intent' }), which turns off the look-ahead that fetches the code of the actions in view on touch screens. It shows what the two save an interaction, and what they cost a load.

idioms.choice: The core loads as a module in <head>, with a modulepreload link, as the performance guide recommends.
Vite bundles the page's script, and fromGlob(import.meta.glob('./actions/*.js')) registers every action as its own chunk. Vite preloads a chunk's dependencies when it is imported.

The server writes the entry's <script> and <link rel="modulepreload"> tags from Vite's manifest, and the modulepreload polyfill is turned off rather than imported, as the backend integration guide allows. Preloading an action's imports stays on.
The cart header is bound to a store the server serializes (cw-store, cw-bind); cyclewire/signals arrives with the cart action.
The quick view fetches JSON and renders it with cyclewire/dom, which arrives with that action.
The quick view link names its data with cw-prefetch, and the prefetch plugin fetches it on intent, next to the action's code; the action's ctx.fetch() takes that response.

start({ preload: 'intent' }) fetches an action's code only on intent, on every screen: the look-ahead that the default ('auto') runs on touch screens, fetching the code of the actions in view once the page is idle, is off. The server writes <link rel="modulepreload"> for the entry and its imports only.
The build and the actions are the CycleWire app's: this folder has its own entry, which imports ../cyclewire/src/actions/*.js, and resolve.dedupe keeps one copy of cyclewire.
